counterfactual_missing_items: R2 has no raw support span for lung adenocarcinoma metastasis to the liver.
No raw evidence of a metastatic pattern or recurrent lung disease favoring R2.
No raw evidence of ovarian-type stroma or other features that would favor mucinous cystic neoplasm over IPNB.
decisive_items: Biliary cytology revealed papillary adenocarcinoma in situ or papillary adenoma with severe atypia.
The cystic lesion was suspected to be a mucin-producing biliary tumor, such as a mucinous cystic neoplasm of the liver or an intraductal papillary neoplasm of the bile duct.
Endoscopic retrograde cholangiography demonstrated obstruction of the right hepatic bile duct, compression of the left hepatic duct, and dilation of peripheral bile ducts.
response.rationale: R4 is directly supported by multiple raw spans: ERC shows biliary obstruction/compression, the lesion is suspected as a mucin-producing biliary tumor, and biliary cytology shows papillary adenocarcinoma in situ or severe atypia. C1 is an append-only completion of R4 that adds subtype wording but relies on the same cytology span, so it is discounted as a correlated restatement. R2 has no raw support and is contradicted by the biliary imaging and cytology findings.

rejected.why: Correlated append-only completion of R4; its only raw support span is already used by R4 and adds no independent evidence.
No raw support spans; the remote lung adenocarcinoma history is a generator opinion and is outweighed by biliary obstruction, mucin-producing tumor suspicion, and papillary cytology.
